target.title: fix(logging): warn when configured file writes fail
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators using a configured log file could lose file logs without any diagnostic when appends failed. Blank persisted `logging.file` values were also accepted as canonical config even though they could never identify a writable file.

N/A (no existing issue)

## Why This Change Was Made

The logger now reports the first failed append in each uninterrupted failure episode and retries subsequent writes without flooding stderr. A successful append clears the warning latch; successful rotation does not, because rotation alone does not prove that writes recovered.

Blank values are repaired at the configuration owner boundary rather than by a permanent runtime fallback: `openclaw doctor --fix` removes an existing blank `logging.file`, and canonical validation rejects new blank values without trimming or otherwise transforming nonblank paths.

## User Impact

Operators now receive a concise stderr warning when the configured log file cannot be written. Once the path becomes writable, logging recovers without a restart; a later independent failure is reported again. Existing blank values have a doctor migration to the default log path, while valid configured paths keep their exact bytes.

## Evidence

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Failed file appends were swallowed and the returned failure signal was ignored, so OpenClaw could continue running while silently losing file logs. Blank persisted paths also remained malformed canonical configuration.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux x86_64, Node 24.14, branch `fix/logging-silent-file-write-failure`, head `56599e3457ff38c6683b52224757ae9974ccfe1a` rebased onto `upstream/main` `ffff72c43aedf5bdeb32a6836f577850207f8573`.
- **Exact steps or command run:** `node --import tsx /tmp/verify-logging-file-failure.mjs`
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture of the `node` runtime verification (copied live output):

  ```text
  schema blank rejected=true; doctor removed=true; migrated valid=true
  consecutive failure warnings=1
  recovery append=true; exact path exists=true
  warnings after recovery and new failure=2
  ALL PASS
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** Canonical validation rejects blank paths; doctor removes a shipped blank value while preserving sibling logging settings; two consecutive append failures emit one warning; a successful append recovers logging; and a later failure emits a new warning.
- **What was not tested:** A packaged OpenClaw deployment on a read-only container filesystem. The append-failure contract was exercised deterministically by placing a directory at the configured file path, then removing it to prove recovery on the same logger instance.

### Tests and checks

```text
OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/config/logging-file-empty.test.ts \
  src/commands/doctor-legacy-config.migrations.test.ts \
  src/logging/log-file-silent-failure.test.ts \
  src/logging/log-file-size-cap.test.ts \
  src/logging/logger-settings.test.ts

Test Files  5 passed (5)
Tests       77 passed (77)
```

Additional checks completed successfully:

- core production and core test `tsgo` lanes
- scoped `oxfmt` and `oxlint`
- conflict-marker check
- runtime import-cycle check: 0 cycles
- `git diff --check`
